move: full-bleed slides, white wipe with push, captions rise, progress fills
how: Square stage with five full-frame photo slides stacked, only one visible at a time. Each slide lasts 20% of the loop: its image drifts in a different direction (xPercent/yPercent +/-3, scale up to 1.1, linear), its caption rises from an overflow mask (yPercent 110 to 0, expo.out 0.8s) 0.3s in and its subtitle fades in from x -20, then both leave (caption yPercent -110 expo.in) 0.5s before the segment ends. Five thin progress bars fill left to right (scaleX, linear) one per segment. The transition at each segment boundary is a white wipe: a full-frame white plane scales from left over 0.4s (expo.inOut), the next slide is set visible and the old one hidden under it, the new slide pushes in from x 120 (expo.out 0.7s) while the wipe collapses toward the right. The fifth segment wipes back to slide one, and the progress bars reset 20ms before the end so the loop closes.
adapt: Swap the five images, captions, subtitles and the HUD strings; N slides derives the segment length automatically. Keep the 0.4s expo.inOut wipe, the 0.7s push and the drift amplitude.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the deck slides, wipe plane, HUD and progress bars inside el and sets slide 1 visible. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with SEG = D/N; the fromTo calls already carry immediateRender:false so the build order is safe.
caveats: catalog says 13s but render.json duration is 10s
transitions rely on .set() opacity swaps, which are seek-safe but not reversible mid-wipe if you scrub backwards across several
